PRINCIPLE: Each test should focus on a single requirement/behavior with one Arrange-Act-Assert. RATIONALE: Single-focus tests make root cause identification precise. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if the test exercises exactly one method call/behavior with one clear arrange-act-assert; non-compliant if multiple act operations or multiple scenarios are combined. DECISION RULES: (1) Count distinct 'Act' operations: this test calls pilha0.empilha(...) and pilha0.desempilha() (two acts) so >1 -> non-compliant. (2) Test name does not indicate multiple operations but the presence of both push and pop is sufficient for non-compliance per rule 1. VERDICT: non-compliant because it performs two distinct operations in the same test method.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should not depend on other tests or execution order. RATIONALE: Independence allows arbitrary execution order and parallel runs. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Look for @Before/@After usage or that tests use only local variables. DECISION RULES: No @Before/@After present but the test uses only local variables and does not modify shared/static state -> compliant. VERDICT: compliant because the method uses only local state and no shared mutable state is visible.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Coverage of Normal and Exceptional Flows
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Tests should cover both happy path and error scenarios. RATIONALE: Ensures robustness and exception handling. EVALUATION CRITERIA: There should be at least two test methods per behavior (happy path + error case) or explicit exception assertions. DECISION RULES: This class shows only a single happy path test; no @Test(expected=...) or assertThrows usage and only valid inputs are used -> non-compliant. VERDICT: non-compliant because no exceptional/error flow is tested for the method under test.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should validate min/max and just-outside boundaries. RATIONALE: Many bugs occur at boundaries. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Look for empty, zero, negative, max values or test names indicating edge cases. DECISION RULES: This test uses typical operations only and does not check empty stack behavior or other boundary cases -> non-compliant. VERDICT: non-compliant because no boundary (e.g., empty stack, pop-on-empty) checks are present.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should be self-contained and reuse helper methods/constants. RATIONALE: Reduces duplication and improves maintainability. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Look for helper methods/constants or short tests without duplication. DECISION RULES: The test is short (<10 lines) and does not duplicate code across multiple methods (only one method shown) -> compliant. VERDICT: compliant because the method is short and self-contained.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Detailed Analysis of Size and Complexity

EVALUATION CRITERIA: Test methods <20 lines, no loops/complex conditionals. DECISION RULES: This test is short (~5 lines) and contains no loops or conditionals -> compliant. VERDICT: compliant due to small size and simple linear flow.

PRINCIPLE: Assertions should be comprehensive and verify multiple properties. RATIONALE: Superficial assertions may miss faults. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if multiple properties of the result are asserted (>=2) or collection size plus contents. DECISION RULES: This test contains only one assertion (assertEquals(0, tamanho())) -> non-compliant. VERDICT: non-compliant because it performs only a single, superficial assertion rather than verifying multiple properties (e.g., returned value from desempilha and size).
